guides.title: Save your planner
guides.headline: Save your planner, somewhere safe.
guides.intro: Your files are ready the moment you check out, on your confirmation page and in your email.
guides.clipNote: Downloading the file and saving it to Files

default: Open your order email or the confirmation page after checkout, and tap the download link.
Save the PDF to your device. On iPad choose Save to Files; on Android it goes to your Downloads folder.
Keep this original. Import a copy into your app and leave this file untouched as your clean backup.

guides.tip: Download the files on the device you will plan on. It saves a step later.

guides.cardText: Add your planner to your app.
guides.title: Import it into your app
guides.headline: Import it into your app.
guides.intro: Bring the planner into the app you will write in. Always import the original PDF so every link keeps working.
guides.clipNote: Importing the planner into the app

default: Open your notes app and find its Import option.
Choose the PDF you saved in step 1.
Wait for the import to finish before closing the app, so no pages go missing.
goodnotes: Open GoodNotes and go to your Documents.
Tap New, then Import, and choose the PDF you saved in Files.
Wait for the import to finish before you close the app.
notability: Choose the PDF you saved in Files.
Wait for the import to finish before you close the app.
samsungnotes: Tap the PDF import button and choose the planner from My Files or Downloads.
Wait for the import to finish before you close the app.

guides.tip: Import the file as one PDF. Importing pages separately is the most common cause of pages out of order.

guides.cardText: Jump between pages with a tap.
guides.title: Use the links
guides.headline: Learn how the links work, in two minutes.
guides.intro: Every page in your planner is linked. Once you know where the links are, you will never scroll to find a page again.

default: Tap any date, tab or button on a page to jump straight to it. Tap once; don't draw on it.
If nothing happens, switch to reading mode. The pen writes; the hand or reading tool taps links.
Tap the three lines at the top right of any page to get back to the index.
Tap the logo at the bottom of any page to close the planner and return to the cover.

guides.tip: Most link problems come from having the pen tool selected. Switch tools and try again.

guides.title: Set up your basics
guides.headline: Set up your basics, once.
guides.intro: A few settings make writing feel natural from the first page. Everything else is already built in.

default: Turn on palm rejection in your app's settings, then rest your hand on the screen normally.
Set your pen to about 0.7mm and slow down slightly. Your digital handwriting improves faster than you think.
Write your name on the Info page.

No copying pages needed. All 12 months, 52 weeks and 365 days are already in your planner, dated or undated. Logs come with their own linked pages too, like a recipe log where every entry opens its own recipe page.

guides.tip: Pressure sensitivity needs a pressure-sensitive stylus, like Apple Pencil or S Pen.
undatedSteps: Date your planner. Pick the month you want to start with, write it at the top of the first monthly page and fill in that month's dates. Then date each week and day as you reach it, a few weeks ahead at most, so your planner stays flexible if plans change.

guides.title: Plan your first week
guides.headline: Plan your first week, start to finish.
guides.intro: Put it all together: from the month, into the week, down to today.
guides.clipNote: Planning a week from the monthly page

default: Open this month with the tabs on the right.
Tap the W number for this week to open the weekly page.
Add your weekly tasks and the habits you want to track.
Tap today's date to open the daily page and choose your three top priorities.

guides.tip: Spend five minutes on Sunday with the weekly page. The rest of the week plans itself.

guides.title: Set your dates
guides.headline: Set your dates, your way.
guides.intro: For undated planners: start in any month and fill in the dates yourself.
guides.clipNote: Writing in the dates on an undated month

default: Choose your start month and write it on the first monthly page.
Fill in the dates on the month grid.
Add the dates to each week as you reach it.

guides.tip: Only date a few weeks ahead. It keeps the planner flexible if plans change.

guides.title: Duplicate or add a page
guides.headline: Duplicate or add a page.
guides.intro: Need another notes page or template? Copy one instead of starting from scratch.

default: Open the page overview in your app, where you see all the pages as thumbnails.
Choose the page you want another copy of, and select Duplicate.
Move the copy next to the page it belongs with.

guides.tip: Links point to the original page, so keep the original where it is and move the copy.

guides.title: Use your stickers
guides.headline: Use your stickers, any set.
guides.intro: Every Lilac Desk sticker set works the same way.
guides.clipNote: Adding a sticker and resizing it

default: Save the sticker file to your device.
Add it to your app's stickers or images, then place a sticker on the page.
Select it with the lasso tool and drag the corner handles to resize.

guides.tip: Sticker won't move? It may be on a locked template layer. Add it to a new layer or page instead.

guides.title: Back up your planner
guides.headline: Back up your planner, just in case.
guides.intro: Keep your plans safe if your device is lost or replaced.

default: Turn on cloud sync or backup in your app's settings.
Sign in to the same account on every device you use.
Keep the original PDF saved somewhere separate as a clean copy.

guides.tip: As long as sync was on, a new device just needs the app and your sign-in.

faq.q: My links aren't working. What do I do?
faq.a: Tap the link once; don't draw on it. If nothing happens, you're in editing mode, so switch to reading (hand) mode. Also check that you imported the original PDF, not a flattened copy.

faq.q: How do I add my planner to my app?
faq.a: Save the PDF to your device, then use your app's Import option and choose the file. The Import it guide has the steps for your app.

faq.q: Can I use it on more than one device?
faq.a: Yes. Turn on cloud sync in your app and sign in to the same account on each device. Give it a minute on Wi-Fi to catch up.

faq.q: What is the difference between dated and undated?
faq.a: Dated planners have 2027 printed on every page. Undated planners leave the dates blank, so you can start in any month.

faq.q: Should I customize the original file?
faq.a: No. Duplicate it first and customize the copy. That way you always have a clean original to fall back to.
Yes. Export the page as a PDF, then print at 100% or actual size on A4 or US Letter.

faq.q: Can I share my planner with others?
faq.a: These are for your personal use, so please don't redistribute or resell the files. Sharing your own filled-in pages with family or on social media is totally fine.

problems.q: My handwriting looks messy on screen
problems.fix: Completely normal for the first two to three weeks. Increase your pen thickness to 0.7mm and slow down slightly. Your digital handwriting improves faster than you think.

problems.q: I can't write on my planner at all
problems.fix: Your file most likely opened in a plain PDF viewer instead of your planner app. Import it into your annotation app (GoodNotes, Notability, Xodo and so on), then make sure the pen tool, not the hand or reading tool, is selected.

problems.q: My palm keeps leaving marks
problems.fix: Turn on palm rejection in your app's settings, then rest your hand on the screen normally. It's designed to ignore it.

problems.q: My stylus isn't being detected
problems.fix: Check your stylus is charged and paired (for Bluetooth pens) or seated properly (for passive styluses). Restart the app after reconnecting. Most writing issues clear up after a fresh launch.

problems.q: Every line looks the same thickness
problems.fix: Pressure sensitivity needs to be turned on in your app's pen settings, and it only works with a pressure-sensitive stylus like Apple Pencil or S Pen. A plain capacitive stylus won't do it.

problems.q: There's a delay when I write
problems.fix: Close other apps running in the background and make sure your device's software is updated. Lag is almost always a performance issue, not a planner issue.

problems.q: The tabs won't jump between pages
problems.fix: Tap the tab once; don't draw on it. If nothing happens, you're in editing mode, so switch to reading (hand) mode. Also confirm you imported the original hyperlinked PDF, not a flattened copy.

problems.q: The links on the cover or index don't work
problems.fix: Same fix as the tabs: you're likely in editing mode. Switch to the hand or reading tool, and confirm you imported the original file rather than a screenshot or flattened copy.

problems.q: My pages are out of order
problems.fix: This happens when pages import separately. Re-import the original PDF as a single file, or open the page manager and drag the pages back into order.

problems.q: I can't find the file I imported
problems.fix: Check your app's main library or Documents view and search for the planner's name. Make sure the import fully finished before you closed the app.

problems.q: The planner looks blurry
problems.fix: Zoom to 100% before you judge it. Screen previews often look soft. If it's genuinely low resolution, re-download the original PDF and import it again.

problems.q: The colors look different from the photos
problems.fix: This is almost always your screen, not the file. Brightness, dark mode and color profile all shift how colors look. Turn off dark mode and check in daylight before comparing.

problems.q: It looks stretched, cropped or the wrong shape
problems.fix: Your app may have fit the page to a different shape. Look for an original size or fit to page import setting and choose the one that keeps the file's real dimensions.

problems.q: A sticker won't move or resize
problems.fix: Select the sticker with the lasso tool first, then drag the corner handles. If it won't budge, it may be on a locked template layer. Add it to a new layer or page instead.

problems.q: My plans aren't syncing across devices
problems.fix: Confirm cloud sync is switched on and that you're signed in to the same account on both devices. Give it a minute on Wi-Fi to catch up.

problems.q: The app crashed and I lost my work
problems.fix: Most apps auto-save every few seconds. Reopen the app and check your recent files, or look for recovery files in the app's settings.

problems.q: I lost or replaced my device
problems.fix: As long as cloud sync was on, reinstall the app on your new device and sign in. Your files should come right back.

problems.q: My storage is full and the import won't finish
problems.fix: Free up space on your device or in your cloud account before re-importing. A partial import is the most common cause of missing or out-of-order pages.

problems.q: The app won't open at all
problems.fix: Restart your device first. It fixes more than you'd expect. If that doesn't work, check the app store for a pending update.

problems.q: I lost my download
problems.fix: Open your order email or your order confirmation and download the files again. Can't find it? Message me with your order number and I'll send it over.

problems.q: I want to print a page
problems.fix: Export the page as a PDF, then print at 100% or actual size on A4 or US Letter for a clean result.

problems.q: My printed page is cut off at the edges
problems.fix: Turn off fit to page or scale to fit in your print settings and print at 100% or actual size instead. Scaling is almost always the cause.

problems.q: I want to share my plans with family
problems.fix: Export the pages as a PDF or image, or share the whole file through a cloud link.

problems.q: Can I share these planners with others?
problems.fix: These are for your personal use, so please don't redistribute or resell the files. Sharing your own filled-in pages with family or on social media is totally fine.
